# Execution Plan

The Awtsmoos renews the river, yet no wave may falsely claim the sea;
Awtsmoos.com moves from proof to owner to rewrite to proof, until the graph is free.

## Phase One — Baseline testimony

- Run the two auto-scroll Node tests unchanged.
- Run imported-style ownership and CSS-quality baselines.
- Confirm the port-8080 listener PID, command, HTTP identity, and canonical route response.
- Trace every import/caller/test for `richCommentWarmup` and prove whether real dependencies reach it.

## Phase Two — Cold Community proof

- Stop only a process proven to be the Awtsmoos application, never tunnel infrastructure.
- Restart through the package-defined application entry and capture logs outside product source.
- Measure startup warmup result, first Chitas `/comment-tree`, second identical request, and a nonexistent fixture control.
- If latency is defective, isolate packed-store open, manifest readiness, root-index read, native tree traversal, imported aggregation, and serialization using external profiling first.
- Rewrite a whole owner only after the measured cause is known; leave no temporary diagnostics behind.

## Phase Three — Reader behavior witness

- Discover the current Chrome target afresh and navigate via real rendered routes.
- At 390x844 prove document scroll topology and measure countdown cancel, running movement, pause stability, resume movement, Stop stability, restart, pace mutation, and clean document end.
- Search production routes for a true inner scroll vessel; accept one only if geometry, overflow, and actual `scrollTop` movement prove it.

## Phase Four — Overlay and accessibility sweep

- Enumerate Main Menu registrations from runtime/source and exercise every child path on phone and desktop.
- Exercise every Scribe's Lens control, persistence/reset, focus order, internal scrolling, Escape/close, safe-area, and reduced-motion behavior.
- Verify floating controls never overlap or intercept beneath overlays.
- Repair layer ownership, never by arbitrary z-index escalation.

## Phase Five — CSS ownership and route inventory

- Build the active post CSS closure from template links plus recursive imports.
- Map ownership for floating controls, scroll roots, sidebars, sheets, modals, comments, fixed positioning, dimensions, z-index, focus/hover/active/disabled, and safe-area padding.
- Classify historical owners ACTIVE / DORMANT / LEGACY / DEAD / COMPATIBILITY before removal.
- Inventory Heichel and Social entrypoints, renderers, bootstraps, CSS roots, APIs, overlays, and scroll ownership.

## Phase Six — Heichel and Social browser sweep

- Heichel: 390x844, 430x932, 768x1024, 1440x900; LTR/RTL; long/short titles; cards/series/posts/menus/loading/empty/error/modal/focus/overflow/network/console.
- Social: root scope, feed, profile, composer, notifications, reactions, comments, following, discovery/search, rails, empty/loading/error, mobile/desktop, focus/press/hover/reduced-motion/overflow/network/console.

## Phase Seven — Evidence-led whole-file repairs

For every reproduced defect: read the complete owner and imports; preserve public contracts unless runtime disproves them; rewrite the complete source file; split oversized responsibilities; use tabs and full readable layout; add no `!important`, specificity escalation, or global catch-all fix; then run syntax, targeted tests, browser reproduction, and regression search.

## Phase Eight — Completion closure

- Rerun required suites and newly discovered relevant scripts.
- Re-scan active CSS closure, social scoping, debug residue, focus, reduced motion, horizontal overflow, fixed/z-index collisions, stale pace/storage assumptions, touched-file line counts, and indentation.
- Re-read every modified source file in full.
- Compare 0240 plan vs actual source vs runtime proof.
- Create non-colliding implementation-readback, browser-verification, and final-delta completion files in the original 0240 folder.
- Run takeover and embarrassment tests; every actionable answer re-enters REMAINING_WORK.

## Source-touch policy

No production file is pre-authorized for change. The first likely candidate is the rich-comment startup warmup boundary because its observed dependency contract appears inconsistent with its observed caller; that remains a hypothesis until call-path and runtime evidence prove it.

## REMAINING_WORK

The 18-item ledger in `00-reality-and-inheritance.md` remains authoritative and open.

## NEXT_ACTION

Run auto-scroll/style baselines and prove the rich-comment warmup caller contract, then update the ledger from receipts.
